problem_text:
A telecommunications company is tasked with establishing a fiber-optic ring network connecting seven major data hubs. The geographic coordinates for each hub are as follows:
Hub Alpha: (199,158)
Hub Beta: (9,10)
Hub Gamma: (69,41)
Hub Delta: (38,149)
Hub Epsilon: (74,92)
Hub Zeta: (101,140)
Hub Eta: (33,75)

The required cable lengths, measured in kilometers, for potential direct links between hubs have been surveyed:
Alpha to Gamma: 174.9 km
Alpha to Delta: 161.3 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 141.4 km
Alpha to Zeta: 99.6 km
Alpha to Eta: 185.6 km
Beta to Gamma: 67.5 km
Beta to Delta: 142.0 km
Beta to Epsilon: 104.6 km
Beta to Zeta: 159.3 km
Beta to Eta: 69.3 km
Gamma to Delta: 112.4 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 51.2 km
Gamma to Zeta: 104.0 km
Gamma to Eta: 49.5 km
Delta to Epsilon: 67.4 km
Delta to Zeta: 63.6 km
Delta to Eta: 74.2 km
Epsilon to Zeta: 55.1 km
Epsilon to Eta: 44.4 km
Zeta to Eta: 94.1 km

Due to a regulatory restriction, a direct cable connection between Hub Alpha and Hub Beta is prohibited and cannot be constructed. Furthermore, the network design must incorporate exactly one of two specified critical links: either the connection between Hub Beta and Hub Gamma, or the connection between Hub Gamma and Hub Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total cable length required to create a continuous ring that interconnects each data hub precisely once and returns to the initial hub.
